rv.q: The music justifies the long buildup, and the play, Adjmi’s best so far, is as rich and lustrous as they come.

Stereophonic is constructed out of those hypernaturalistic details, with each little frustration along the way to an album building on the next, like a fugue, up to the points when those songs start to come together, the play breaks open, and, against all indications, incandescent art comes out.
But they cannot make up for the slackness of the play, which fundamentally adds up to a moderately sudsy and soporific trawl through that familiar trinity: sex, drugs and rock ’n’ roll.
Does Stereophonic rock? It does, hard.

David Adjmi’s Stereophonic, a phenomenal new play with gorgeous music by Arcade Fire’s Will Butler premiering at Playwrights Horizons, doesn’t avoid these clichés so much as drown them out with far more interesting narratives.
Stereophonic is a must-experience, rather than simply a must-see.
Stereophonic is very much a commanding theatrical and musical experience.
The three-hour running time zooms by.
Beautiful and unwieldy, mesmerizing and frustrating, it’s way too long for its own good, but I savored every moment.
Stereophonic delivers an amply rewarding portrait of how musical sausage is made.
In terms of fresh ideas about the creative process, the play doesn’t deliver an LP’s worth of insights.
Those moments in Stereophonic felt far too few.
But why we have to be locked in here for over three hours, only Adjmi knows.
This is a wild, thrilling ride.
The creative energy and compounded exhaustion that live inside every brilliantly performed song cause Stereophonic to sing, most magnetically...

Playwright David Adjmi (The Evildoers, Stunning and Other Plays), has struck platinum with his astounding Stereophonic, a hybrid comedy/drama/musical, currently running at Playwrights Horizons through December 17.
Stereophonic has been extended through Dec. 17 at Playwrights Horizons (416 West 42nd St.).
The results may not be Rumours-level genius

cn.t: Critics largely praise this immersive three-hour drama about a '70s rock band recording an album, citing stunning music by Will Butler and meticulous craft, though some find its deliberate pacing overly long and indulgent.

vr.q: I love this play. I cannot recommend it enough.
Last night I saw Stereophonic at Playwrights Horizons and it was amazing
